question.problem:
What division problem is represented by the model below?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14129811/assets/b2e5fb40e703cb3d93f22fd315852930eaab540445e3f570e8de3dacfdc83e0b.png)
question.worked_solution:
We have $\dfrac{1}{4}$ on the left and $\dfrac{1}{8}$ on the right.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14129811/assets/785deacac749a6ed43e5e6a2638677e8ff9e9b58087cb4e471ea85fd50609ce6.png)

The division operation splits the shaded region on the left into $2$ equal parts. So the shaded part on the left is $2$ times larger than the shaded part on the right.

Therefore, the division problem shown is:

$$
\dfrac{1}{4} \div 2 = \dfrac{1}{8}
$$
